subject: Home improvement
hook: HOME IMPROVEMENT IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Home improvement isn’t a modern fad – it dates back to ancient Rome, where 1st‑century B.C. entrepreneur Sergius Orata invented the hypocaust underfloor‑heating system
angle_support: Professional home improvement is ancient and goes back to the beginning of recorded civilization.
One example is Sergius Orata, who in the 1st century B.C. is said by the writer Vitruvius ... to have invented the hypocaust.
title: Roman Underfloor Heating: The Original Home Improvement Hack
description: The idea that home upgrades are a modern trend is wrong. Romans used under‑floor heating centuries ago, thanks to entrepreneur Sergius Orata, who turned it into a profitable real‑estate strategy.
narration: HOME IMPROVEMENT IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You think home improvement is a modern DIY craze. It was actually a lucrative business in ancient Rome, driven by wealthy entrepreneurs like Sergius Orata in the 1st century B.C. Vitruvius records that 1st‑century B.C. merchant Sergius Orata invented the hypocaust—an under‑floor heating network that warmed wealthy Roman villas. He bought cheap villas, installed his system and spas, then flipped them for profit across the empire. Ancient heating shows home upgrades have always been profit‑driven and innovative.
